texts.preamble: Mehndi Hasan & 3 Ors. vs State Of U.P. Thru Secy. Home & 4 Ors. on 20 September, 2019 Author: Anil Kumar Bench: Anil Kumar, Saurabh Lavania High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Court No. - 3 Case :- Misc. Bench No. - 870 of 2007 Petitioner :- Mehndi Hasan & 3 Ors. Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru Secy. Home & 4 Ors.
texts.facts: The present petition has been filed for the following main reliefs:- "i. a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opposite parties i.e. opposite party no. 4, not to make any interference or hindrance in peaceful functioning and carrying on the business of the petitioners of slaughtering and selling buffalow's meet in village Saddipur, P.S. Jahangirabad, District Barabanki. ii. a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opposite party no. 2 and 3 to take suitable action against the opposite party no. 4 with respect for complaint made by the petitioners through representation dated 7.12.2006 and 14.12.2006 contained in Annexure Nos. 1 and 2 to this writ petition." On behalf of opposite party no. 5, Sri Virendra Kumar Shukla has accepted notice. In the meantime, it is provided that in case no bye-laws has been framed by the Zila Panchayat and there are no statutory rules or valid executive orders for restraining the petitioners from slaughtering and selling the buffalo meat at the particular place, the petitioners' business shall not be interfered with." The petition seeks issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus directing respondent No.4 (Station House Officer, P.S. Kotwali, district Barabanki) not to create hindrance in functioning and carrying business of the petitioners of slaughtering and selling buffaloes' meat in village Alapur, P.S. Kotwali, district Barabanki. In the meantime, it is provided that in case no bye laws has been framed by the Zila Panchayat and there are no statutory rules or valid executive orders for restraining the petitioners for slaughtering and selling the buffalo's meat at the particular place, the petitioners' business shall not be interfered with. "
texts.arguments: Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that in an identical matter, on 02.08.2019 the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No. 7701 of 2008 (Hazi Hasan and two others Versus State of U.P. Thru Secy. Home and 4 Others) , has passed the order. 3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has pointed out that there has been a development in so much as the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 provides for making application for grant of licence for slaughtering the buffaloes and selling its meat. Learned counsel contends that in the further development, the petitioners applied for licence on 25.4.2017. However, neither licence has been granted nor the petitioners are being allowed to pursue their profession. 4. Learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh, however, has pointed out that a new Act, viz Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017 has come into force. The petitioners are required to make an application under the provisions of the Amendment Act of 2017. The Court has been further assured that in case an application for grant of licence is filed under the Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017, decision thereon would be taken within a period of four weeks of making the application.
